clue.text: Tool cauterises wound after third of stitches removed

indicators.note: wound is the past tense of wind, as in twisted round, so the remaining letters are twisted into a new order
removed tells us a letter is taken out of the word cauterises before it is shuffled
third of points to the third letter of the word stitches

explanation.surface: A surgeon's tool seals a wound once some of the stitches have been taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking I (third letter of 'stitches') out of CAUTERISES leaves CAUTERSES, and 'wound' shuffles that into the answer. 'Wound' reads as the injury, but here it is from the verb wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are pruning shears, a gardening implement for cutting stems.

clue.text: Country: a second where Lesotho located?

indicators.note: located says the other pieces are set within the South Africa letters, as Lesotho is set within that country

parts.note: Lesotho is an enclave entirely surrounded by South Africa, abbreviated SA
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A quiz question: name a country, then say in a second where Lesotho is.
explanation.walkthrough: Lesotho is a small kingdom wholly enclosed by South Africa, which makes the containment picture apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an island nation in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Joker maybe behind screens in a Catholic's office

indicators.note: to screen is to shield or hide, so the card and lateness words together enclose the small words

parts.note: a joker is an example of a playing card
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: A joker hides behind screens in a Catholic church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joker' is not a prankster but a playing card, and 'behind' means overdue rather than at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinalate is the rank or office of a cardinal in the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: One or two fliers?

parts.note: the single bird's name is made of two other bird names joined, a small songbird and a skylark

explanation.walkthrough: TIT and LARK are each birds, and together they name one bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A titlark is a pipit, a small brown songbird whose name combines two bird names.

clue.text: Singular noun arranged around punctuation mark, shortly

indicators.note: around says the rearranged noun letters go round the shortened punctuation word
arranged means the letters of noun are put into a new order
shortly means the punctuation word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a comma is a punctuation mark

explanation.surface: A grammar note: a singular noun is placed around a punctuation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' makes UNON from noun; 'Singular' means remarkable here, not the grammatical number the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular in the sense of remarkable or unusual, a synonym for uncommon.

clue.text: Shed somewhere in Berkshire

definitions.meaning: to cast off, as a snake sheds its skin
A town in Berkshire, a county west of London

explanation.definitionFit: Slough is a Berkshire town, and to slough skin is to shed it.

clue.text: Grant fed cold sweet

indicators.note: the grant is fed, so it takes the cold letter inside itself like food

parts.note: a dole is a handout or grant of money
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone called Grant was given a chilled dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a man's name, but it is a common noun meaning a handout.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce is the Italian musical direction meaning to be played softly and tenderly, literally sweetly.

clue.text: Doctor nursed a performer

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor gave nursing care to an entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a medic but is the verb meaning to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, a stage performer.

clue.text: Round of bloomers in sport? Certain to be eliminated

indicators.note: to be eliminated says the word for certain is removed from the longer word

parts.note: sport is a leisure pursuit, hence the query
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A garland in a sporting event, where one competitor is sure to be knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' are flowers, not underwear: a ring of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland, a ring of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: Short bursts help me, saving time

indicators.note: saving here means keeping inside, so the shuffled letters hold the time word
something that bursts breaks apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Brief outbursts of help me save time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bursts' shuffles HELP ME to EPHEML, which holds ERA. 'Short' is the definition, not part of the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting a very brief time, so short-lived.

clue.text: Value in flag, patriotism finally returning

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters come back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: to flag is to tire, to lose energy

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word patriotism

explanation.surface: A nation's flag is valued as a symbol of patriotism coming back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns TIREM (TIRE plus M) backwards. 'Flag' is the verb meaning to weaken, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, so value is a close synonym.

clue.text: Swimmer's incompetent first of four splits

indicators.note: the first letter of four splits the other word apart by going into its middle

parts.note: clownish means clumsy and inept, like a clown

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word four

explanation.surface: A poor swimmer comes apart after one of a group of four falls behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer's' is 'Swimmer is': the definition, then a link. F from 'four' goes inside CLOWNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A clownfish is a small brightly striped reef fish, so it is a creature that swims.

clue.text: Plate knocked over: drawer for it?

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned the other way, so the plate word is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer
magnetism is the force that draws things towards it, so it is a drawer in the sense of one that draws

explanation.surface: A plate gets knocked over: is the thing that pulls it in responsible?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is not furniture but something that draws or attracts. 'It' as a definition is the old slang for sex appeal, as in an It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is slang for sexual attractiveness, which is exactly the raw personal allure called animal magnetism.

clue.text: Put away at home, box packed with extraordinary care

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: packed with means the box is filled with the other letters

parts.note: a crate is a box

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters of care are rearranged

explanation.surface: Store something at home in a box packed with exceptional care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' makes ARCE from care. 'Put away' looks like tidying but means jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away is slang for to imprison, which is to incarcerate.

clue.text: Eccentric, if excellent corporation

parts.note: crack means first-rate, as in a crack shot
corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, as is pot

explanation.surface: It sounds odd, but suppose a corporation were excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is the humorous term for a large paunch, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person with odd ideas.

clue.text: Ancient study with group of horses he painted

parts.note: con is an archaic verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a stable is the set of horses kept by one owner

explanation.surface: An old study of horses, done by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter, famous for The Hay Wain, which includes horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Constable is the English painter John Constable, so the man who painted.

clue.text: Two rums originally in strong drink

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two of something, as in a brace of pheasants

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the word rums

explanation.surface: A pair of rums go into a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' here is only a link: the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracer is a stiff, fortifying alcoholic drink that braces you up.

clue.text: Name torn from Chinese book chap pens — one of fifty

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the chap word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a man is a chap

indicators.note: torn from says the letter for name is ripped out of the book title

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese Book of Changes

explanation.surface: A man writes after tearing a name from a Chinese book.
explanation.walkthrough: The I Ching is the ancient Chinese divination text; 'torn from' leaves ICHIG once the N goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Michigan is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Subtlety is missing from pest

indicators.note: missing from says the small word is absent from the longer one, so its letters are dropped

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A clever observation that something has vanished from a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning, a subtle distinction.

clue.text: Increase status in competition

indicators.note: in places the status word inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup
rank is status or standing

explanation.surface: Raise one's standing in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To crank up is to increase or intensify, as with volume.

clue.text: Circulating quickly around system, chocolate eggs initially in gut

indicators.note: around tells us the first word goes round the initials, enclosing them

parts.note: something viral spreads fast, as a video does online

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of system, chocolate and eggs

explanation.surface: Chocolate eggs pass quickly through the digestive system and end up in the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulating quickly' suggests the bloodstream, but it means spreading like a viral video.
explanation.definitionFit: Visceral feelings are deep instinctive ones, felt in the gut rather than reasoned.

clue.text: Tropical plant schmuck dipped in wine

indicators.note: dipped in means plunged into, so the fool word goes inside the wine

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
a schmuck is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A tropical plant that some idiot dunked in wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava is a tropical shrub grown for its starchy root.

clue.text: Seen in pebbledash, large piece of masonry

indicators.note: seen in means the answer is visible spanning the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something spotted in pebbledash: a big chunk of stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: Pebbledash is a rough wall render studded with small stones, common on British houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is squared, dressed stone used in building, or a block of it.

clue.text: Sensing fine things, a fine thing indeed!

definitions.meaning: literally, a cat's whiskers are sensitive organs that feel delicate things nearby
the idiom means something excellent, the very best

explanation.definitionFit: The cat's whiskers is an idiom for something superb, and literally a cat's whiskers are fine sensory hairs.

clue.text: Splendid wave

explanation.definitionFit: Swell is old slang for marvellous and also an ocean billow.

clue.text: Best of British beer good after siesta

indicators.note: after says the beer and good pieces come behind the siesta piece in the answer

parts.note: a siesta is a rest, a break
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A proud British boast: nothing beats a beer after an afternoon nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best of British' is short for the phrase 'the best of British luck', a good-luck wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Break a leg is the theatrical way of wishing a performer good luck, as is the best of British.

clue.text: Bird: I'm not sure able in the end to soar?

indicators.note: in a down answer, soaring means rising up the column, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation, of not being sure

indicators.note: in the end picks the final letter of the word able

explanation.surface: Is this bird able to soar in the end? I'm not sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To soar' reads UME upward in this down answer; the surface teases a bird that cannot fly at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Notice what women often don't give in saying

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
a jokey reference to the stereotype that women won't reveal their age

explanation.surface: Observe what women often won't reveal when they speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a proverb or traditional saying.

clue.text: Bone ultimately funny in arm

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word bone

parts.note: a funny is a joke, a quip

explanation.surface: The funny bone, finally found in the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the funny bone at the elbow. 'Arm' is a verb meaning supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm is to equip, supply with weapons or gear.

clue.text: Take one back, possibly, as may master for servant?

definitions.meaning: something that rings a bell sounds familiar and may carry you back to a memory
a master would literally sound a bell to summon a servant

explanation.definitionFit: To ring a bell is to stir a memory, and literally to sound a summoning bell, as masters once did.
